newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Red Cross to send flour to North Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Red Cross to send flour to North Korea.

text.p: The South Korean Red Cross said on Wednesday it would ship 500 tonnes of flour to impoverished North Korea on Friday.
The aid worth 178 million won ($200,000) was donated by South Korean religious groups, including Christians and Buddhists.
It will be shipped from the port of Inchon to the North Korean west coast city of Nampo on a third country vessel, Red Cross official Lee Jong-geun said.
Famine is looming over North Korea after two consecutive years of massive floods and economic collapse.

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has launched an appeal for $41.6 million in food aid for the Stalinist state. South Korea has pledged $6 million and the U.S. $10 million, and the first shipment is scheduled for May.

South Korean food aid to North Korea was frozen after a Northern submarine infiltrated 26 commandos into the South last September. It resumed after Pyongyang apologised for the incursion last December.
Polticial analysts expect more aid will flow as Seoul and Washington try to lure Pyongyang to proposed peace talks, which would also include China.
"If North Korea comes to the table and we start making progress on four-party talks this could be one of the main and early issues under discussion," said one Seoul-based Western diplomat.
The South Korean Red Cross is the only permitted channel for private aid to North Korea from the South.
WFP representatives who visited North Korea last week said Pyongyang would need to import at least 2.3 million tonnes of grain for 1997 to ward off famine.
